title: Richard M. Jones and his last Decca recording
summary: Dominique worked with Jones in Chicago and New Orleans, made his last record with him, and defends his ability to write music.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: There's a couple other men here. Richard M. Jones, Miney. Miney Jones.

I worked with him in Chicago. I worked with him in New Orleans. Well, you know yourself. My last recording was with Richard Miney Jones on the Decca Company. That was the last record I made with Jimmy Noon and Johnny Dodson. And both of them died.
I never heard him play much piano solos. Was he good on piano?

Very good on solos. Moneyy Jones could play some nice solos with him. Very good. He composed a lot of numbers. And he'd write it too. A lot of people didn't think Moneyy Jones knew music. But he'd write out that music. Moneyy Jones. I'm not going to down him. Another boy I worked with in New Orleans too, he's in that nice pal, but I don't know if he played with Walter Decker.
Oh no. He's still living. Still living.
No Walter's still living? Yeah. He looked simple.
